entities.blurb: An allay is a small flying passive mob that follows the player who has given it an item, or any note block it has heard in the last 30 seconds. It searches for and collects dropped instances of its held item and drops them near the player or note block it is currently following.
entities.name: Allay

entities.blurb: An armadillo is a passive mob found in badlands and savannas. It rolls up in response to being hurt or being near undead mobs or players that are sprinting or mounted. While in this state, it takes less damage. It also repels spiders and cave spiders. It is the only source of armadillo scutes, which the armadillo sheds over time, as well as when it is brushed.
entities.name: Armadillo

entities.blurb: An axolotl is a passive aquatic mob found in lush caves that hunts most other aquatic mobs, and can assist players with aquatic combat and grant them Regeneration. They can also be carried around in a bucket.
entities.name: Axolotl

entities.blurb: A bat is a flying passive mob that spawns in dark areas. It is the only ambient mob in the game, intended to complement the game's atmospheric settings.
entities.name: Bat

entities.blurb: A bee is a flying arthropodan neutral mob that lives in a bee nest or beehive, and fills it with harvestable honey using nectar it gathers from flowers. Attacking a bee, or interfering with its home without proper precautions, causes it and all nearby bees to attack using their stingers. If a bee attacks something, it will lose its stinger and eventually die.
entities.name: Bee

entities.blurb: A blaze is a fiery hostile mob found in Nether fortresses and is the only source of blaze rods. It attacks by shooting volleys of three small fireballs or by performing melee attacks at close range, and it often floats upward while targeting a player.
entities.name: Blaze

notes.content: Only when killed by a [[player]] or a tamed [[wolf]].
notes.name: player_or_pet

entities.blurb: A bogged is a mushroom-covered skeleton variant that spawns in swamps and mangrove swamps. Bogged behave similarly to skeletons, but have less health, fire their bows more slowly, take damage from powder snow, cannot convert to strays, and shoot tipped arrows of Poison.
entities.name: Bogged

notes.content: Only when killed by a [[player]] or a tamed [[wolf]].
notes.name: player_or_pet

entities.blurb: A breeze is a hostile mob spawned by certain trial spawners found in trial chambers. It moves via jumping large distances when attacking, attacks by firing wind charges, and deflects all projectiles that hit it except wind charges. Breezes are the only source of breeze rods, which are dropped upon death.
entities.name: Breeze

notes.content: Only when killed by a [[player]] or a tamed [[wolf]].
notes.name: player_or_pet

entities.blurb: A camel is a large passive mob found in deserts and desert villages. They can be saddled and ridden by up to two players at once. When standing, it is tall enough that its riders cannot be reached by most melee-attacking mobs on the ground.
entities.name: Camel

entities.blurb: A camel husk is an undead variant of the camel that rarely spawns at night or during thunderstorms in deserts as a hostile mob, being ridden and controlled by an iron spear-wielding husk with a parched passenger, known as a camel husk jockey. It does not burn in sunlight, and is passive once separated from its riders.
entities.name: Camel Husk

entities.blurb: A cat is a passive mob found in villages and swamp huts. They can be tamed and creepers and phantoms are afraid of them.
entities.name: Cat

entities.blurb: A cave spider is a smaller spider variant that naturally spawns in sulfur caves. It behaves similarly to a normal spider, but has less health and inflicts Poison with its melee attacks on Normal and Hard difficulty.
entities.name: Cave Spider

entities.blurb: A chicken is a passive mob found in most grassy biomes, and the main source of raw chicken, feathers, and eggs. They have three variants based on the temperature of the biome they spawn in.
entities.name: Chicken

entities.blurb: Cod are common bucketable aquatic passive mobs found in oceans that are a source of raw cod and, occasionally, bones‌[Bedrock Edition  only] or bone meal.‌[Java Edition  only]
entities.name: Cod

entities.blurb:
A copper golem is a buildable passive mob that takes items out of copper chests, and attempts to store them in nearby wooden chests and trapped chests. A chest examined by a copper golem must either be empty, or contain the item type it is holding, for the golem to place anything inside of it. 
If not waxed, a copper golem oxidizes over time and eventually turns into a copper golem statue, dropping its currently held items.
entities.name: Copper Golem

entities.blurb: A cow is a passive mob found in most grassy biomes and are a source of leather, beef, and milk. They have three variants based on the temperature of the biome they spawn in.
entities.name: Cow

entities.blurb: A creaking is a hostile mob spawned by active creaking hearts at night. It moves to attack players with melee headbutts, but cannot move at all while any players in Survival or Adventure mode can see it. It is protected from all damage by the creaking heart that spawned it; breaking the creaking heart kills the creaking. Hitting a protected creaking causes resin clumps to grow on pale oak logs near its linked creaking heart.
entities.name: Creaking

entities.blurb:
A creeper is a common hostile mob that quietly approaches a player, hisses, and explodes if the player remains near. Creeper explosions can destroy blocks and deal massive amounts of damage, which can be completely blocked using a shield or blocks.
When struck by lightning, a creeper becomes a charged creeper, which amplifies its explosion power and enables mob heads to be obtained from piglins, zombies, skeletons and other creepers it kills. It also bumps up the chance for a wither skeleton skull to drop to 100% from a wither skeleton.
Due to its distinctive appearance and unique destructive method of attack, the creeper has become one of the most iconic mobs of Minecraft, being featured in promotional material and merchandise.
entities.name: Creeper

notes.content: The disc is randomly selected from [[Music Disc 13|13]], [[Music Disc cat|cat]], [[Music Disc blocks|blocks]], [[Music Disc chirp|chirp]], [[Music Disc far|far]], [[Music Disc mall|mall]], [[Music Disc mellohi|mellohi]], [[Music Disc stal|stal]], [[Music Disc strad|strad]], [[Music Disc ward|ward]], [[Music Disc 11|11]], and [[Music Disc wait|wait]].
notes.name: random_disc

notes.content: Only when killed by a [[charged creeper]].
notes.name: charged_creeper

entities.blurb: Dolphins are aquatic neutral mobs that live in non-frozen oceans. They grant a speed boost to players that swim near them and follow the player while swimming.
entities.name: Dolphin

entities.blurb: A donkey is a passive mob similar to a horse that, when tamed, can be saddled, ridden, and equipped with a chest to transport items.
entities.name: Donkey

entities.blurb: Drowned are common neutral underwater zombie variants that spawn in oceans, rivers, and dripstone caves, or when zombies drown. They primarily attack through melee attacks, but may also come armed with tridents that they can throw at range. A baby drowned is referred to as a gurgle.
entities.name: Drowned

entries.note: Adult drowned wielding a trident have a 50% chance of spawning mounted on a [[zombie nautilus]].

notes.content: Only when killed by a [[player]] or a tamed [[wolf]].
notes.name: player_or_pet

entities.blurb: An elder guardian is a large hostile mob and a variant of the guardian. It is the largest and strongest aquatic mob. It attacks the same way as a normal guardian, and it also applies Mining Fatigue to players in a large radius around itself. They are only found in ocean monuments; three of them generate in each one.
entities.name: Elder Guardian

entities.blurb:
The ender dragon is a giant flying hostile boss mob found when first entering the End. It is the largest naturally spawning mob in the game. Its attacks involve charging at the player and shooting fireballs that create damaging effect clouds. The ender dragon can be re-summoned by placing four End crystals around the exit portal.
Defeating the ender dragon the first time activates the exit portal which allows safe return to the Overworld. Each time it is defeated, an End gateway is created on the outskirts of the central island which can be used to teleport to the outer End islands.
entities.name: Ender Dragon

labels: {{Animate|Dragon Fireball JE2.png; Dragon Fireball BE.png|16px}} Dragon fireball

entities.blurb: An enderman is a neutral mob found in all three dimensions that has a chance of dropping ender pearls when it is killed. It becomes hostile to players that damage it or look directly at its face, using its arms to attack. Endermen teleport erratically, as well as away from dangers such as lava, projectiles, and water. They also occasionally pick up and move certain blocks.
entities.name: Enderman

entities.blurb: Endermites are small arthropod hostile mobs that attack by biting. They have a 5% chance to spawn  when a player throws an ender pearl. Endermen are hostile toward endermites.
entities.name: Endermite

entities.blurb: An evoker is a spell-casting illager that can be found in woodland mansions and as part of raids. They are the only source of totems of undying. Evokers use two spells to attack; one that summons armor-piercing fangs and one that summons vexes. This is the only way for vexes to spawn (without using Creative mode or commands).
entities.name: Evoker

entities.blurb: A fox is a trusting, neutral mob found in taigas and similar biomes. It hunts small animals, can carry items in its mouth, and eats anything that is edible. A fox trusts and defends a player that spawned it through breeding, but flees from non-sneaking players in any other circumstance.
entities.name: Fox

entities.blurb: A frog is a passive mob found in swamps and mangrove swamps. It performs large jumps, swims, and uses its long tongue to eat small slimes and small magma cubes. Froglights are created when frogs eat magma cubes; different frog types create different froglight colors.
entities.name: Frog

entities.blurb: Ghasts are large, floating, ghost-like hostile mobs found in the Nether, and are the only source of ghast tears. Ghasts wander aimlessly and shoot explosive fireballs at players, which can be hit back to kill them instantly upon direct impact.
entities.name: Ghast

entries.note: Only 5% of spawn attempts succeed.
Only 5% of spawn attempts succeed.
Only 5% of spawn attempts succeed.

notes.content: Only when killed by a player-deflected [[fireball]].
notes.name: player_fireball

entities.blurb: A giant is an unused over-sized monster mob in Java and Legacy Console editions that resembles a zombie.
entities.name: Giant

entities.blurb: A glow squid is a squid variant that spawns in dark underwater areas, typically in ocean depths, canyons, and underground lakes. It has an aqua luminescent texture, and is the only source of glow ink sacs.
entities.name: Glow Squid

entities.blurb: A goat is a neutral mob found in certain mountainous biomes. It can jump especially high and is milkable. Goats occasionally ram other mobs and players, and cannot be provoked. Ramming into certain blocks causes a goat horn to drop from an adult goat if it has any.
entities.name: Goat

entities.blurb: Guardians are aquatic hostile mobs that spawn in ocean monuments. They attack with a slow-charging laser beam, and inflict retaliatory damage when damaged by a melee attack.
entities.name: Guardian

entities.blurb: A happy ghast is a passive counterpart of ghasts that can be harnessed and ridden by up to four players at once as a flying mount. It can also be used in conjunction with leads to airlift and transport boats and leashable mobs.
entities.name: Happy Ghast

entities.blurb:
Hoglins are breedable hostile mobs found in the Nether, and a source of porkchops and leather. Hoglins are repelled by warped fungi that is placed in the world as well as active Nether portals and respawn anchors. They attack by thrusting their tusks upward, which can also launch their target a short distance into the air.
Baby hoglins behave similarly, but have a much weaker attack with normal knockback, and flee when hit.
entities.name: Hoglin

entities.blurb: A horse is a passive mob that can be ridden when tamed and saddled, and can wear horse armor. Different horses have different running speeds, jump heights, and health points, and these attributes can be inherited and improved through breeding.
entities.name: Horse

entities.blurb: Husks are a variant of the zombie that spawn in deserts. They function similarly to zombies, except that they do not burn in sunlight, and they inflict Hunger with their unarmed attacks.
entities.name: Husk

entries.note: Husks have a 10% chance of spawning wielding an [[iron spear]] mounted on a [[camel husk]] with a [[parched]] passenger.

notes.content: Only when killed by a [[player]] or a tamed [[wolf]].

entities.blurb: The illusioner is an unused illager armed with a bow. It attacks by firing arrows and creating illusions.
entities.name: Illusioner

entities.blurb: An iron golem is a buildable neutral mob that attacks monsters with its arms, knocking them into the air. Iron golems are spawned by villagers to patrol and protect their villages. Iron golems spawned by villagers will retaliate against players if attacked, and are hostile to players that have low popularity or reputation with their village.
entities.name: Iron Golem

entities.blurb: A llama is a tameable neutral mob that can be equipped with a chest to transport items, and can wear carpets for decoration. If attacked, it will retaliate using its spit.
entities.name: Llama

entities.blurb: A magma cube is a hostile mob found in the Nether. A magma cube behaves similarly to a slime in that it splits into smaller magma cubes on death, all the way down to tiny size, but is fireproof, jumps higher and less often, and deals more damage. Magma cubes are a source of magma cream and the only source of froglights if eaten by a frog while small.
entities.name: Magma Cube

notes.content: Only if magma cube size is medium or big.
notes.name: medium_cube

notes.content: Only when ''not'' killed by a [[frog]].
notes.name: not_frog

notes.content: Only when killed by a [[cold frog]].
notes.name: cold_frog

notes.content: Only when killed by a [[temperate frog]].
notes.name: temperate_frog

notes.content: Only when killed by a [[warm frog]].
notes.name: warm_frog

entities.blurb: Mannequins are mob-like entities that resemble a player's avatar without having a connected player.
entities.name: Mannequin

entities.blurb: A mooshroom is a mushroom-covered variant of the cow exclusive to the mushroom fields biome. Mooshrooms are a great source of mushroom stew and leather.
entities.name: Mooshroom

entities.blurb: A mule is a passive mob created by breeding a horse and a donkey together. It is very similar to a donkey, except that it cannot breed.
entities.name: Mule

entities.blurb: A nautilus is a neutral mob that can be tamed, saddled, and ridden as an underwater mount that can dash and protects the rider from drowning. With no rider, it uses its dash to hunt pufferfish and to briefly retaliate if attacked. It can also be equipped with nautilus armor.
entities.name: Nautilus

notes.content: Only when killed by a [[player]] or a tamed [[wolf]].
notes.name: player_or_pet

entities.blurb: An ocelot is a trusting, passive mob found in jungles. They run away from nearby players, but their trust can be gained by feeding them raw cod or raw salmon. Creepers, as well as phantoms in Bedrock Edition, stay away from ocelots.
entities.name: Ocelot

entities.blurb: A panda is a rare neutral mob that resides in jungles. Certain aspects of a panda's behavior and appearance vary depending on its personality.
entities.name: Panda

notes.content: [[Mojira:MC-160006|MC-160006]]
notes.name: MC-160006

entities.blurb: A parched is a skeleton variant that spawns in deserts. Parched behave similar to skeletons, but have less health, do not burn in sunlight, fire their bows more slowly, take freeze damage instead of converting to strays, and shoot tipped arrows of Weakness.
entities.name: Parched

entities.blurb: A parrot is a tamable passive mob that spawns in jungle biomes. Parrots imitate sounds of nearby monsters and can perch on the player's shoulders.
entities.name: Parrot

entities.blurb: Phantoms are flying undead hostile mobs that spawn in the night sky when the player has not slept in a bed or straw bed​[upcoming: Third Drop 2026] or died for at least 3 in-game days. They attack by diving at the player from the sky to bite them.
entities.name: Phantom

entities.blurb: A pig is a passive mob found commonly in most grassy biomes. Adult pigs are a source of porkchops and can be ridden using a saddle and a carrot on a stick. They have three variants based on the temperature of the biome they spawn in.
entities.name: Pig

entities.blurb:
A piglin is a neutral mob found in the Nether. It is hostile to players unless they wear at least one piece of golden armor. It can be given gold ingots to barter for various items. It wields either a golden sword, a golden spear, or a crossbow and uses either melee, spear charge, or ranged attacks, respectively. 
Baby piglins do not grow up, are passive, and take gold without giving anything in return.
entities.name: Piglin

notes.content: Only when killed by a [[charged creeper]].
notes.name: charged_creeper

entities.blurb: A piglin brute is a hostile and stronger variant of the piglin. It wields a golden axe and appears in all types of bastion remnants. Unlike piglins, piglin brutes do not barter, retreat, or get distracted by gold.
entities.name: Piglin Brute

entities.blurb: A pillager is an illager armed with a crossbow found in wandering patrols, in pillager outposts, or as a participant in raids. It attacks by firing arrows at the player.
entities.name: Pillager

notes.content: Only when the pillager is a [[raid captain]] and is not participating in a [[raid]]. Its level is randomized from 1 to 5.
notes.name: leader

notes.content: Only when the pillager is a [[raid captain]] and is not participating in a [[raid]]. Its level is randomized from 1 to 5.
notes.name: leader

entities.blurb: Polar bears are large neutral mobs that live in icy biomes. Adult polar bears are protective of their babies, attacking players that get too close or attack any babies near them.
entities.name: Polar Bear

entries.note: Despite attempts to spawn, it cannot spawn here in Java Edition.

entities.blurb: Pufferfish are bucketable aquatic neutral mobs found in oceans. Although they never seek out mobs to attack, they defensively inflate themselves when approached too closely by players, axolotls, or non-aquatic mobs, dealing damage and inflicting Poison on them.
entities.name: Pufferfish

entities.blurb:
A rabbit is a passive mob found in many snowy and forested biomes, as well as deserts. It runs away from players that are not holding its food, and is able to jump over fences. Rabbits are a source of raw rabbit, rabbit hide, and rabbit's feet.
The Killer Bunny is a hostile rabbit variant exclusive to Java Edition that can only be spawned using commands.
entities.name: Rabbit

entities.blurb: A ravager is a large hostile mob that only spawns alongside illagers during raids. It attacks players, adult villagers, wandering traders, and iron golems by charging, biting, and roaring at them. A ravager can sometimes become stunned if its attack is blocked with a shield.
entities.name: Ravager

entities.blurb: Salmon are common bucketable aquatic passive mobs found in oceans and rivers that are a source of raw salmon and, occasionally, bones‌[Bedrock Edition  only] or bone meal.‌[Java Edition  only]
entities.name: Salmon

entities.blurb: A sheep is a common passive mob that supplies wool and raw mutton and is found in most grassy biomes.
entities.name: Sheep

notes.content: Color of dropped wool corresponds to color of sheep. A sheared sheep does not drop wool when killed.
notes.name: wool

entities.blurb: A shulker is a cubic hostile mob found only in End cities. It hides in its shell to protect itself and blend in with its surroundings, and attacks by shooting homing bullets that inflict Levitation. It is the only source of shulker shells, which are used to craft shulker boxes.
entities.name: Shulker

entities.blurb: Silverfish are small hostile arthropods found infesting stone and deepslate blocks in mountain caves and certain structures, such as strongholds, or spawned using potions of Infestation. They attack by biting, and attacking one can cause nearby silverfish to break out of their blocks to attack the aggressor.
entities.name: Silverfish

entities.blurb: Skeletons are common undead hostile mobs that perform ranged attacks with a bow, shooting arrows from a distance. They are most commonly found in the Overworld at night or in dark locations, but also spawn in the Nether in soul sand valleys, and occasionally in Nether fortresses. They are an important source of bones and arrows, which they drop upon death.
entities.name: Skeleton

notes.content: Only when killed by a [[charged creeper]].
notes.name: charged_creeper

entities.blurb:
A skeleton horse is an undead skeletal horse that sometimes spawns from lightning strikes during thunderstorms, as a skeleton trap. When this trap is approached, it transforms into four skeleton horsemen. A skeleton horse becomes passive once separated from its skeleton rider, and can then be ridden. Unlike most undead mobs, skeleton horses do not burn under direct sunlight.
A skeleton horseman is a skeleton with an enchanted bow and enchanted iron helmet riding and controlling a skeleton horse.
entities.name: Skeleton Horse

entities.blurb: Slimes are cube-shaped hostile mobs that spawn deep underground in particular chunks, aboveground in swamps, or when an Oozing-affected entity dies (unless it's a slime). They move by jumping, chasing after their targets, and usually dealing damage on touch. Slimes spawn in different sizes, and larger ones split into smaller ones on death. Slimes are a major source of slimeballs.
entities.name: Slime

entities.blurb: A sniffer is an ancient passive mob that spawns only by hatching from sniffer eggs. It looks for and digs up torchflower and pitcher plant seeds in dirt, grass, and moss blocks.
entities.name: Sniffer

entities.blurb: A snow golem is a buildable passive mob that throws snowballs at monsters, which provokes them to attack it. Depending on the biome temperature, it also either produces a trail of snow or takes heat damage and dies.
entities.name: Snow Golem

entities.blurb: A spider is a neutral wall-climbing arthropod (arachnid) that attacks players on sight in dark areas by jumping and biting them. Spiders drop string and spider eyes upon death.
entities.name: Spider

entities.blurb: A squid is a common aquatic passive mob that spawns in rivers and oceans, and is the main source of ink sacs, which it drops upon death.
entities.name: Squid

entities.blurb: A stray is a skeleton variant that spawns in various snow-covered biomes. They behave very similarly to skeletons, except they fire tipped arrows of Slowness from their bows and do not freeze in powder snow.
entities.name: Stray

entities.blurb: A strider is a passive mob found in the Nether. It can walk on lava and be saddled by the player, being directed via a warped fungus on a stick. They can be fed warped fungus to breed, and are a source of string.
entities.name: Strider

entries.note: Adult striders have a 3.3% chance to spawn being ridden by a zombified piglin holding a warped fungus on a stick.
Adult striders have a 3.3% chance to spawn being ridden by a zombified piglin holding a warped fungus on a stick.

entities.blurb:
A sulfur cube is a bucketable jumping passive mob that is found only in sulfur caves. It can absorb a full-sized block into itself, which immobilizes it and makes it receive higher knockback from most attacks instead of damage. The block type a sulfur cube absorbs affects its bounciness and behavior, and some blocks cannot be absorbed, such as slabs and stairs. Blocks can be extracted using shears, by replacing the block with a different one, or by killing the sulfur cube.
Small sulfur cubes spawn in groups of two when a large sulfur cube dies. They grow up over time similarly to babies and cannot absorb blocks.
entities.name: Sulfur Cube

entities.blurb: A tadpole is a bucketable aquatic baby passive mob hatched from frogspawn. They mature into one of the three frog variants depending on the biome in which they mature.
entities.name: Tadpole

entities.blurb: A trader llama is a llama variant that spawns in pairs leashed to wandering traders. It behaves similarly to a regular llama, but becomes hostile if the wandering trader is attacked, and will despawn when the trader does unless the lead is removed.
entities.name: Trader Llama

entities.blurb: Tropical fish are common bucketable aquatic passive mobs found in warm or lukewarm oceans, mangrove swamps, and lush caves. There are 2,700 naturally occurring variants of tropical fish of different colors and shapes with unique names in Bedrock Edition and 3,072 in Java Edition.
entities.name: Tropical Fish

entities.blurb: Turtles are passive mobs found in beach biomes. They can be bred with seagrass and lay turtle eggs. They are the only source of turtle scutes, which drop from baby turtles when they mature into adults, and can be used to craft turtle shell helmets.
entities.name: Turtle

notes.content: Only when not killed by [[lightning]].‌[[[Bedrock Edition|Bedrock Edition]] only]

entities.blurb: A vex is a small flying hostile mob that wields an iron sword and is summoned by evokers. It attacks by lunging at its target with its sword and is capable of phasing through walls.
entities.name: Vex

entities.blurb: Villagers are humanoid passive mobs that inhabit villages, work at their professions (see Villager professions), breed, and interact with each other. Their outfit varies according to their occupation and biome, and a player can trade with them using emeralds as currency, with their prices affected by reputation.
entities.name: Villager

entities.blurb: A vindicator is an illager equipped with an iron axe. Vindicators spawn in woodland mansions and participate in raids. They sprint toward their targets to attack them with their axe.
entities.name: Vindicator

entities.blurb: A wandering trader is a passive mob similar to villagers that sometimes spawns near players, alongside two trader llamas tied to it with leads. It can be traded with, buying commonly available resources and selling items mostly native to specific biomes. Its trades are randomized each time it spawns, and it will despawn after enough time has passed.
entities.name: Wandering Trader

entities.blurb: A warden is a hostile mob summoned by sculk shriekers which are located in the deep dark. It is completely blind, relying entirely on vibrations and its sense of smell to detect players and entities to attack, and digs down to despawn if it does not detect anything for 60 seconds and if it doesn't have a name. If a warden successfully detects a target, it rapidly strikes them with its arms, or fires damaging sonic beams which pass through blocks and ignore armor, shields, and all enchantments. A warden will always drop one sculk catalyst and five experience points.
entities.name: Warden

entities.blurb: Witches are hostile mobs that use potions in combat, using various splash potions for offense and drinkable potions for defense.
entities.name: Witch

entities.blurb: The wither is an undead boss mob spawned by building a specific structure using soul sand or soul soil and three wither skeleton skulls. It is able to fly, fires explosive blue and black skulls at players and most non-undead mobs, and becomes immune to some types of projectiles when it is below half health. It is the only source of Nether stars, which are needed to craft beacons.
entities.name: Wither

entities.blurb: A wither skeleton is a tall, black variant of a skeleton equipped with a stone sword. They inflict the Wither effect when attacking the player. They are found exclusively in Nether fortresses and are the only source of wither skeleton skulls, as well as the only renewable source of coal.
entities.name: Wither Skeleton

notes.content: Only when killed by a [[charged creeper]].
notes.name: charged_creeper

entities.blurb: A wolf is a neutral mob that can be tamed using bones. Tamed wolves defend their owners against attackers and can assist in combat. Wolves can also be equipped with wolf armor, but only if tamed.
entities.name: Wolf

behavior.text: Neutral (wild, or if owned by a different player)

entities.blurb: A zoglin is an undead hostile mob that a hoglin turns into when out of the Nether for fifteen seconds straight. It never retreats or flees, and attacks players and almost all non-zoglin mobs indiscriminately, using the same tusk attack as its non-zombified counterpart.
entities.name: Zoglin

entities.blurb: A zombie is a common undead hostile mob that deals melee damage and is a source of rotten flesh, which it drops upon death.
entities.name: Zombie

entities.blurb: A zombie horse is an undead variant of the horse. It rarely spawns in dark areas as a hostile mob being ridden and controlled by a zombie horseman wielding an iron spear. It becomes passive once separated from the zombie rider, allowing it to be tamed and ridden.
entities.name: Zombie Horse

behavior.text: Passive{{note|Passive by itself, but hostile as a jockey, as the rider control its pathfinding, therefore making it hostile, despite zombie horses not actually damaging players, like small slimes.}}

entities.blurb: A zombie nautilus is an undead variant of the nautilus that spawns being ridden and controlled by a trident-wielding drowned, forming a zombie nautilus jockey. Once separated from the jockey, it behaves like a regular nautilus, but burns in sunlight instead of suffocating while not in water.
entities.name: Zombie Nautilus

entities.blurb: A zombie villager is a variant of the zombie that can be cured into a normal villager by using a golden apple on it while it is under the effect of Weakness.
entities.name: Zombie Villager

entities.name: Zombified Piglin
